minutes.headline: Task force agreed to try an April Green Communities grant application, led by a sewer pump and drive project.
minutes.summary: The Green Community Task Force met jointly with town facilities, library and planning/zoning members. Most of the meeting covered whether a project could be ready for the April grant round, with the sewer pump and drive replacement as the lead candidate, plus charging stations, library HVAC and heat pumps, and a draft energy storage bylaw. The minutes were moved and seconded as amended, and the chair tabled the committee structure discussion and wanted another meeting before the end of the month.

votes.motion: Accept the prior minutes as amended, removing the two sentences about the application dates.

budget_items.what_was_said: Grant periods are April and October, a town can apply once a year, and the April round is described as less competitive than October.

budget_items.topic: Sewer pump motors and drives grant
budget_items.what_was_said: A couple of pumps could reach the grant maximum, and the project may be split into motors and drives.
The Sewer Commission has retained earnings that would fund the project, so it would not need town meeting appropriation; money for pumps was also put in the budget.
A suggestion to take a small amount from the grant application for a hybrid police cruiser, with the rest for the pump motors or drives.
Chargers range from a low-cost unit to a dual charger with a pole; the grant would pay for infrastructure up to the charger while the town pays for the charger.
Payment would run through a vendor who likely charges a card-style processing fee.
Quotes from the first contractor were called astronomical even with rebates, and other quotes are being sought.
Members were unsure whether a town's grant maximum drops after cumulative awards reach a threshold; the chair will ask the state contact.
Federal funds are being awarded to other states; the state has not yet applied, and much may flow through Mass Save.
The draft requires a removal bond capped at a percentage of the estimated removal cost.

decisions.decision: Members agreed the most logical path is to pursue the sewer pump and drive project for the April grant round, if the application can be completed in time.
Informal consensus to include a small hybrid cruiser item in the application alongside the pump project.
Chair tabled the committee structure discussion and will seek another meeting before the end of the month, and will contact the state grant contact about deadlines and the cap.
Chair to propose a new meeting date by email by Friday; members indicated Wednesdays and Thursdays are difficult.

what_happened.line: The task force agreed the most logical path is to pursue a sewer pump and drive project for the April Green Communities grant round, if the application can be finished in time.
Members reached informal consensus to add a small hybrid police cruiser item to the application alongside the pump project.
The chair tabled the committee structure discussion and will seek another meeting before the end of the month; the chair will also contact the state grant contact about deadlines and the grant cap.
The chair is to propose a new meeting date by email by Friday, with Wednesdays and Thursdays difficult for members.
The task force heard a draft energy storage bylaw with planning and zoning members; no vote was recorded, and the outcome of the prior minutes was not audible.

why_it_matters: The sewer pump project would be paid from Sewer Commission retained earnings and a state grant, so it would not need a town meeting appropriation, which keeps it off the general tax levy.
The draft energy storage bylaw, with its removal bond, and the library heat pump and EV charger plans are early-stage items that could later come to residents as bylaw votes or town-funded costs.
